My final answer, `final.py`, scores **82.5** on the search split, using **5 of the 24 scorer calls**. It produced exactly the pairs the reference does on the scored inputs (866 and 545) and on about 460 random tests of my own. Those tests covered empty and whitespace-only records, exact duplicates, mixed whitespace, case differences and very common words.

| Candidate | Search score | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| `cand1.py` | 70.7 | First version: only compares records that could still reach 80 % |
| `cand5_1.py` | 71.1 | Dropped the library imports |
| `cand6.py` | 80.5 | Grouping exact duplicates moved into built-in calls |
| `cand8_4.py` | 81.9 | Word ordering built from every 4th record |
| `final.py` (copy of `cand8_4.py`) | 82.5 | Re-scored; the 81.9 → 82.5 change is run-to-run noise |

**How it works:**
- Records with the same set of words are grouped first and all paired with each other directly.
- Words are ordered from rarest to most common. Records are processed from fewest words to most.
- Only the rarest few words of each record are indexed, since a pair that shares none of them cannot be 80 % alike. Records too short or too long to reach 80 % are skipped.
- Every remaining candidate pair is checked with the reference's exact formula, `5·|A∩B| ≥ 4·|A∪B|`, so the pairs reported are always exact.

**Things worth knowing:**
- **Common words matter a lot.** A version without the rarest-first ordering (`cand7.py`) was 30× slower on my test data where some words are much more common than others. Real catalogue text is likely to look like that, so I kept the ordering even though building it costs about 2 ms per input.
- **The worst case is safe.** If every record shares common words, it falls back to checking roughly as many pairs as the reference does, with similar cost per pair. That should stay well inside the 3× cutoff.
- **I stopped at about 8 ms per input.** Splitting the records into word sets alone takes about 2.5 ms of that, and the reference has to do it too. My last few changes to the main loop measured the same as before.

I left my scratch files in the folder (`cand*.py`, `test.py`, `gen.py`, `prof.py` and a few debug copies).
